acceptance_evidence: One reviewed external source version has an exact registry identity, immutable expected size/SHA-256 and source-version retrieval plan.
Corrupt-byte and wrong-size injection tests prove the final destination is never published on verification failure.
Interrupted local retrieval resumes only from an exact plan-bound contiguous chunk checkpoint and rejects a tampered partial prefix.
Verified retrieval receipt and deterministic retrieval inventory bind the exact source registry without treating retrieval as rights approval.
At least three immutable source versions have independent verified receipts and no duplicate source-version inventory entries.
Maintained fsspec remote/object-store execution is exercised with exact runtime version and no credentials embedded in durable URIs.
Remote interruption/resume is injected and final remote bytes reproduce the registered SHA-256 and size exactly.
Retrieval inventory is handed to the exact corpus-foundation/dedup plan without source-registry identity drift.
Representative multi-source acquisition records throughput, peak memory, bytes transferred, request counts and storage/egress cost where applicable.
Repeated retrieval from the same immutable source-version set produces identical verified artifact hashes and inventory identity.
Expired credentials, truncated streams, unexpected upstream mutation and destination collision all fail closed with no verified final artifact.
A corpus-freeze candidate references an exact verified retrieval inventory plus the independent rights/policy and decontamination evidence owned by their respective gates.
Every retrieved source artifact is reproducible from its exact registered version or has an explicitly preserved immutable snapshot with the same hash.
AUDIT-B independently retests retrieval/inventory identity and rights separation before any corpus-freeze acceptance.
Any materially paid acquisition/storage execution has separate explicit authorization; absent it, only LOCAL_FREE evidence is admissible.
